themes.name: Silent receipt upload failures in low-signal areas
themes.insight: Receipt photos taken offline appear to succeed but silently fail or vanish with no retry or error, leading to lost receipts, extra investigation work, and eroded trust in the app.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Meaning it never made it to me. There's no draft, there's no error, it's just... gone.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Half the time the photo's not in the app anymore.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Once I came back to the app that evening and there was a message that said "upload failed, try again," but the photo was gone, so I couldn't try again.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: So they snap it, and it sits in this "sending" state, and then at some point it decides it's failed and drops it.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: Things just quietly don't go through.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: One of our foremen, Luis, brought me his phone and a crumpled receipt in a sandwich bag. He said, "I don't trust it, so here's both."

themes.name: Rigid approval chains misfit for small teams
themes.insight: The mandatory multi-level approval chain doesn't fit small organizations, forcing duplicate approvals, placeholder approvers, and stalled purchases when an approver is away.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: A nine-dollar parking ticket goes through the exact same three steps as a two-thousand-dollar equipment rental.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Kind of. Lena made a placeholder user called "Studio Approvals" so the chain would save.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: "Why am I approving my own team's coffee twice." [laughs] Fair question.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: A thirty-dollar order of clay sits there for nine days because she's at a conference and the app won't let anyone else step in.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: I tried making a delegate, but the delegate setting only works if the person is at the same "level," and there isn't anyone at Monique's level.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: So every expense comes to me, I approve it, and then it comes to me again as finance, and I approve it again. And I can't merge those.

themes.name: Confusing and opaque card limits and declines
themes.insight: Card limits are layered (monthly, per-transaction, category, budget, pending holds) but the UI shows only one number, so people are declined unexpectedly, often in embarrassing situations, and stop trusting the displayed balance.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: And the screen only shows one number. So I'm looking at four hundred and he's standing at a pump in the middle of nowhere with a truck that's empty.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: And the app doesn't show holds. It just shows what's been charged. So I'm looking at nine hundred left and the card's saying no.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: I've kind of stopped trusting the number on the screen.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: I'm a controller. Controls are my whole job. I didn't find it.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: There's "budgets" and there's "limits," and I genuinely don't know the difference.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: Theo now asks me before every lunch, "am I good?" Which is exactly the kind of message I was trying to stop getting.

themes.name: Accounting sync errors that break coding and tracking
themes.insight: Exports to Xero and QuickBooks drop classes, tracking categories, or grant/job info, miscode lines, and sometimes duplicate entries, even though the mapping screen looks correct, creating manual cleanup that defeats the product's purpose.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: The categories in Ledgerly don't line up with our chart of accounts the way they look like they do.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: But the mapping screen says everything is mapped correctly. That's the confusing part. It looks right and the result is wrong.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: In October, about half came through with no class at all. And a bunch landed in the wrong expense account — materials going into "office supplies."

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: And there were duplicates too. Some expenses synced twice. Same amount, same date, two entries in QuickBooks.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: When Ledgerly sends the expenses over, the grant doesn't come with it.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: She said it's actually more work than the paper forms, because at least the forms had the grant name written on them.

themes.name: Invite and activation emails routed to the wrong person
themes.insight: Onboarding emails went to the account creator, signer, or a generic inbox instead of the actual users, delaying activation by one to two weeks and making the rollout feel sloppy.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: So when you add people, Ledgerly sends them a welcome email, set your password, activate your card, all that.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: I got eighty-something emails in one afternoon. "Welcome to Ledgerly, Tomás!" Eighty times. With other people's names in the body.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: People don't trust a tool if their first experience is "you didn't get invited."

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: All the setup emails — "finish setting up your account," "connect your bank," all of that — went to Walt.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: But three program coordinators never got their invites.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: Check who the emails are going to when someone signs up. Ask.

themes.name: Mobile app usability barriers for field and non-technical users
themes.insight: Some users find the mobile app unusable in real working conditions due to tiny targets, confusing navigation, and frequent logouts, pushing them to the laptop or to workarounds.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The app? For my guys it's unusable. I'm sorry, but it is.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The buttons are tiny. These guys are wearing work gloves half the day.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: And it logs them out. Not every day, but like every few days they open it and it wants a password.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Too many screens to get to one thing. I gave up on it after a couple of days.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: There's a tab that says "activity," and a tab that says "spend," and I went in circles.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: So I do everything on the laptop now and I've deleted it off my phone.

themes.name: Disagreement: mobile app praised as fast and slick
themes.insight: In contrast to complaints about app usability, other users (office-based or desk/phone-centric) love the app's speed and simplicity, suggesting usability depends on user context.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Honestly, I love the app. I know that's probably not what you hear a lot, but for me it's been so much better.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: It's just... fast? It doesn't make me think.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: But the app itself is still my favorite thing finance has ever given us. Like, genuinely.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: The app is the best part. Like, the phone app is genuinely slick.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: The app. Don't touch the app. Whoever designed the phone app, give them a raise.

themes.name: Screen reader inaccessibility of the receipt capture button
themes.insight: The core receipt-capture button and camera shutter lack accessibility labels for VoiceOver, blocking a blind user from the app's primary action and forcing a slow multi-step workaround.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: But the button to take a picture of a receipt — the screen reader just says "button." That's it. No label.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: And on the camera screen itself, the shutter doesn't say anything at all. I'm swiping around trying to find it and it just skips over it.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: It's maybe six extra steps. But it means I'm doing receipts at night in the hotel instead of right there.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: I got a nice reply saying they'd pass it on. That was three weeks ago.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: If I can't do the main thing, I can't use the product the way it's meant to be used. I have to use it some other, worse way.

themes.name: Inconsistent support answers and unclear help content
themes.insight: Support responses were contradictory, generic, or slow, pointing to articles that didn't resolve issues, which leaves admins uncertain about product behavior.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: I got two different answers from two different people.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: What I can't live with is "yes" from one person and "no" from another.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: They sent me an article about the mapping screen.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: My manager asked finance, and finance asked Ledgerly. It took, like, a week to get an answer.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: I read the help article three times.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: I did. They sent me to the mapping page.

themes.name: Users revert to old habits and run parallel systems
themes.insight: When trust in the new tool is shaken, users keep paper, email, texts, or backup photos alongside Ledgerly, doubling work and defeating the tool's purpose.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: If people don't believe the photo went through, they go back to emailing me, and then I've got two systems.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: A few just text me photos of receipts now. Which, fine, I forward them in, but that's me doing data entry at night.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Now I just take a regular photo with my phone camera first, as a backup, and then I do the app one when I'm back in town.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: That's the month, honestly. People doing the new thing and the old thing at the same time.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: One of our music teachers asked me if she should just go back to the paper form.

themes.name: Training and adoption support is thin or not engaging
themes.insight: Training was brief, optional-feeling, or lightly attended, so people relied on self-discovery and the training could not compensate for product failures or missing information.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: We did a training in the break room with pizza. Six people came.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: This one feels optional to them.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: I can tell from the analytics that eleven people opened it.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: You can't laminate your way out of that. [laughs]

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Honestly I figured most of it out by just poking around.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: Fifteen-minute demo at our Monday standup.

themes.name: Misleading setup completion signals
themes.insight: The onboarding checklist showed a green checkmark and a 'done' state even though team members had not actually received invites or been activated.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: The setup checklist they gave us said "invite your team," and it had a nice green checkmark once I'd imported.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: It said done. It wasn't done. Nobody had anything.

themes.name: Spend-limit rules not explained to admins up front
themes.insight: Admins were not told key behaviors (hidden default per-purchase limits, rolling reset dates, holds counting against limits), so they discovered them through failures.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: I thought the limit reset on the first of the month. It doesn't.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Maybe tell people up front about the hotel thing. If I'd known that, I wouldn't have been surprised at dinner.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: Except then there's a per-purchase limit that defaults to something, I think five hundred, which nobody told me about.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: I called our rep. He walked me through a screen I'd never seen, where the per-purchase thing is hidden under, like, "advanced controls."

themes.name: Bright spots: cards, integrations, reporting and offboarding
themes.insight: Despite the problems, users valued having personal cards, quick identity provider setup, automatic offboarding, audit logs, reporting, and visibility into approval status, suggesting a strong core value proposition.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: The cards themselves. People like having their own card instead of borrowing mine.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The reporting on the website is nice. I can see spend by truck, which I've never been able to do.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: When I disable someone in our identity provider, their Ledgerly access goes too, and the card gets frozen.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: And I can see when finance has looked at something, which, before, I had no idea until the reimbursement showed up three weeks later.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: The cards are great, the staff love not waiting for their money.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: I just think it could be great.

themes.name: Approver notification overload
themes.insight: Busy approvers ignore notifications, including Ledgerly's, which compounds approval delays.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: She told me she gets so many notifications that she's started ignoring all of them, including the Ledgerly ones.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: She's busy, so she doesn't complain, she just doesn't approve things. Which is worse. [laughs]

themes.name: Rollout timing and external context
themes.insight: Some stalls come from organizational context such as concurrent audits, office moves, new hires, and busy seasons, not just the product.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: We're also moving offices in December, so everyone's a bit frazzled. I wouldn't blame Ledgerly for everyone's mood.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Oh, and we hired four people last month, so a lot of folks are new to everything, not just this.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: Oh, we rushed it. We rolled it out the same week as a big safety audit, so nobody had any attention left.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Busy, yeah. Fall's always heavy for us, everybody's stocking up before the holidays.

themes.name: Contractors and non-standard users excluded from the card program
themes.insight: Some groups, such as contractors, cannot yet be issued cards, so teams maintain a split process with old reimbursement methods.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: Not yet. They're contractors, so we're still figuring out whether that's allowed with our insurance.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: For now they buy things and I pay them back the old way, which is a little awkward next to staff who have shiny new cards.
